CFML Language Reference: Tags

CFSTOREDPROC

CFSTOREDPROC runs a procedure stored in the database itself. Nested CFPROCPARAM tags pass its parameters and CFPROCRESULT tags name the result sets it returns. In KoldFusion the tag is recognized, but the built-in flat-file driver has no stored procedures, so every call ends in a Database exception.

Category

Database manipulation

Syntax

<CFSTOREDPROC PROCEDURE="procedure_name"
    DATASOURCE="ds_name"
    USERNAME="username"
    PASSWORD="password"
    DBSERVER="dbms"
    DBNAME="database_name"
    BLOCKFACTOR="blocksize"
    PROVIDER="COMProvider"
    PROVIDERDSN="datasource"
    DEBUG="Yes/No"
    RETURNCODE="Yes/No">
  CFPROCPARAM and CFPROCRESULT tags
</CFSTOREDPROC>

Attributes

PROCEDURE
Required. Name of the stored procedure.
DATASOURCE
Required. Data source to call it in. An unknown data source is reported first.
USERNAME
Optional. Accepted for compatibility; KoldFusion ignores it.
PASSWORD
Optional. Accepted for compatibility; KoldFusion ignores it.
DBSERVER
Optional. Native-driver server name. Accepted for compatibility; KoldFusion ignores it.
DBNAME
Optional. Native-driver database name. Accepted for compatibility; KoldFusion ignores it.
BLOCKFACTOR
Optional. Rows fetched at a time (1 to 100). Accepted for compatibility; KoldFusion ignores it.
PROVIDER
Optional. OLE DB provider. Accepted for compatibility; KoldFusion ignores it.
PROVIDERDSN
Optional. OLE DB data source. Accepted for compatibility; KoldFusion ignores it.
DEBUG
Optional. Accepted for compatibility; KoldFusion ignores it.
RETURNCODE
Optional, default "No". On a native driver, Yes stores the procedure's status code in CFSTOREDPROC.StatusCode. Accepted for compatibility; KoldFusion ignores it.

Usage

The exception has TYPE="Database", CFCATCH.SQLState S1000 and a message explaining that the driver does not support stored procedures. Pages written for an Oracle or Sybase server can catch it and fall back on plain CFQUERY statements, as the example does.

On a server with a native driver, CFSTOREDPROC.ExecutionTime holds the call's duration in milliseconds.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFTRY>
  <CFSTOREDPROC PROCEDURE="sp_GetDeptStaff" DATASOURCE="cfsnippets">
    <CFPROCPARAM TYPE="In" CFSQLTYPE="CF_SQL_VARCHAR" VALUE="Training" DBVARNAME="@dept">
    <CFPROCRESULT NAME="Staff">
  </CFSTOREDPROC>
  <CFCATCH TYPE="Database">
    <CFOUTPUT>
    <P><B>The procedure call failed</B> (SQLState #CFCATCH.SQLState#):<BR>
    <I>#CFCATCH.Message#</I></P>
    </CFOUTPUT>
    <!--- Fall back on a plain query that does the same job --->
    <CFQUERY NAME="Staff" DATASOURCE="cfsnippets">
    SELECT FirstName, LastName FROM Employees
    WHERE Department = 'Training' ORDER BY LastName
    </CFQUERY>
  </CFCATCH>
</CFTRY>
<P>Training department, from the fallback query:</P>
<UL>
<CFOUTPUT QUERY="Staff"><LI>#FirstName# #LastName#
</CFOUTPUT>
</UL>
